### Add feature-loop.sh to grow jvmcontract unattended

[`b54c0ed3a341`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/b54c0ed3a341338599f0e088589f226c23d06b68) · [log `f0cb07435bcd`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b337c438-c453-4e77-9b04-ac89ec125c41/f0cb07435bcde894a45da27038b826a90122b1263f577c53ef7cdef38bdad6df.jsonl.gz)

llm-dlc/tools/feature-loop.sh resumes session 360e8b8b on Fable 5.1 at high effort and repeats one instruction from the repo root: add more advanced features and examples to jvmcontract. Each cycle that produces a commit is followed by /compact and another cycle. A cycle with no new commit stops the loop with exit 1, before compacting, so the session keeps its full context for whoever looks into it. A commit is detected by the change ID of @-, which survives a rewrite of the commit. The README describes the loop.

Verified with a stub claude in a temporary jj repo: two commits then none gave instruction, compact, instruction, compact, instruction, exit 1; no commit on the first cycle stopped at once; a nonzero exit after a commit still continued; SIGTERM exited 130; the script ran at the repo root when started from elsewhere. Fable 5.1 at high effort in auto mode, and /compact in print mode (same session ID, one compact boundary), were checked against the real CLI on a throwaway session outside this repo. The loop itself has not been run against session 360e8b8b.

### Show live progress in feature-loop.sh

[`26835fe0b07f`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/26835fe0b07fc520777a6ca10485738c88b4061b) · [log `582b4cfa3f0c`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b337c438-c453-4e77-9b04-ac89ec125c41/582b4cfa3f0c952e901aa159f278fd98091cbdb207987f3b9648f1728bd8b610.jsonl.gz)

claude -p in text mode prints nothing until a turn ends, so the loop looked hung for hours. It now reads stream-json and prints one timestamped line for each message and tool call, and a closing line with steps, minutes and cost for each turn. The filter skips lines it cannot read, so it cannot kill claude by closing the pipe.

Verified with a stub claude emitting stream-json in a temporary jj repo: progress lines appeared as events arrived, malformed lines were skipped, the stub's exit status 3 was still reported, and commit detection and the stop on no commit behaved as before. The real CLI's result fields were confirmed from a saved run; the stream itself was not run against the real model.

I've added `llm-dlc/tools/feature-loop.sh` and committed it locally as `movtrrpo`, but it hasn't been run against the real session yet. `check` reports 0 errors and 5 warnings, and nothing is pushed.

To start it from anywhere:
```bash
llm-dlc/tools/feature-loop.sh
```

**How it works:** each cycle runs your instruction from the repo root, resuming session `360e8b8b…` with `--model claude-fable-5-1 --effort high`. If that produced a commit, it runs `/compact` and starts again. If not, it exits 1.

**Testing**
- **Control flow:** a stub `claude` in a temporary jj repo gave the right sequence for commits followed by none, no commit on the first cycle, and an interrupt.
- **Real CLI:** on a throwaway session outside this repo, Fable 5.1 at high effort ran in `auto` mode, and `/compact` worked in print mode on the same session ID.

**Decisions I made**
- **No commit means no compact:** the loop stops before compacting, so you keep the full context when you look into why it stopped.
- **Permissions:** it uses `--permission-mode auto`, the mode that session already ran in. Anything that would need a prompt is denied rather than hanging, which could end a cycle with no commit.
- **Failures:** a non-zero `claude` exit doesn't stop the loop by itself; only a missing commit does. A failed `/compact` is logged and the loop continues.
- **Commit detection:** it compares the change ID of `@-`, so a commit that only rewrites the previous one doesn't count as new.
